surprises.body: Los Angeles usually hits more than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 56 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 110 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Turcotte sparks a Kings comeback
paras: What a comeback. Auston Matthews opened the scoring for the Maple Leafs on the power play midway through the first. John Tavares stretched the lead to 2-0 just under five minutes later, and Brandon Duhaime and Corey Perry squared off late in the period. Teddy Blueger and Scott Laughton fought later in the period. The second period was a wild one. Dakota Joshua extended the lead to 3-0 early in the period, but Alex Turcotte got the Kings on the board 21 seconds later. Alex Laferriere pulled the Kings within one on the power play midway through the period, with Erik Gustafsson picking up his 200th NHL assist on the goal. Erik Haula tied it up less than five minutes later. Adrian Kempe scored the only goal of the shootout for the Kings.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Maple Leafs hit a post and the crossbar twice and still lost. Darcy Kuemper settled in after a shaky start for the Kings: he gave up three goals on the first eight shots, then stopped the last 19, and Anthony Stolarz stopped 25 of 28 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Mikey Anderson had the best night of anyone. The Kings improved to 7-11-2, seventh in the Pacific. The Leafs are still last in the Atlantic. They are winless in eight (0-7-1).

items.text: William Nylander passed George Armstrong for seventh on the Maple Leafs’ all-time scoring list, with 715 points.
The Maple Leafs scored on the power play for the first time since Nov 7, after going 0-for-7 over five games.
John Tavares has a point in all seven of his games against Los Angeles since 2023-24.
With Trevor Moore out, Turcotte took his spot and scored.
